q: 1. B.O.D. represents
options: pollution strength of an organic fraction
pollution strength of bio-degradable organic fraction
explain: BOD measures the amount of oxygen required by bacteria to stabilize the *biodegradable* organic matter in water.

q: 2. B.O.D. equation is
explain: The standard first-order reaction equation for BOD exerted at time t is $L_t = L(1 - 10^{-kt})$, where L is the ultimate BOD.

q: 3. In the B.O.D. equation K is called
explain: The constant 'k' (or 'K') represents the rate at which the organic matter is being oxidized (deoxygenation rate).

q: 4. For ordinary domestic sewage B.O.D. reaction is expected to get completed in about
explain: At 20°C, it takes approximately 20 days to complete the first stage (carbonaceous) of the BOD reaction.

q: 5. Usual population equivalent of B.O.D. is
explain: Population equivalent is used to compare industrial waste to domestic sewage; 80g of BOD per person per day is a common design value.

q: 6. B.O.D. test is standardized at
explain: The standard lab test for BOD is conducted at 20°C for a duration of 5 days ($BOD_5$).

q: 7. Light is excluded in B.O.D. incubator to
explain: If light enters, algae will grow and produce oxygen via photosynthesis, which would give a false, lower BOD reading.

q: 8. B.O.D. test is not well suited to industrial wastes because
explain: Many industrial wastes contain toxic substances that kill the bacteria used in the test, making the BOD appear much lower than the actual pollution strength.

q: 9. Second phase B.O.D. is exerted because of the oxidation of ...........
options: carbonaceous matte into CO2 and H2O
explain: The first stage of BOD involves the oxidation of carbonaceous matter. The second stage, known as Nitrification or Nitrogenous BOD, occurs when specialized bacteria (Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter) oxidize ammonia into nitrites and then nitrates.

q: 10. For any waste ...........
options: C.O.D. may be less than B.O.D.
C.O.D. is always greater than B.O.D.
depending upon the percentage of biodegradable matter, it may be either way
explain: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) measures both biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic matter, whereas BOD only measures biodegradable matter. Therefore, COD is always greater than or equal to BOD.

q: 11. Result of C.O.D. is generally higher than that of B.O.D. because ...........
options: the strong oxidising conditions in the test
complete oxidation of organic and inorganic compounds
the stables compounds are being oxidized
explain: The COD test uses a strong chemical oxidizing agent (potassium dichromate in acidic medium), which can oxidize nearly all organic compounds, including those that are biologically resistant (stable), leading to higher oxygen demand values.

q: 12. In a C.O.D. test the most common interference is caused by the ions of ...........
explain: Chloride ions react with silver sulfate (the catalyst) and can be oxidized by dichromate, which leads to falsely high COD results. Mercuric sulfate is usually added to complex the chlorides and eliminate this interference.

q: 13. Time taken for C.O.D. test is about ...........
explain: While a standard BOD test takes 5 days, a COD test is much faster, typically requiring about 2 to 3 hours of refluxing (boiling) to complete the chemical oxidation.

q: 14. An advantage of C.O.D. test over B.O.D. test is ...........
options: it oxidized all matter including toxins
it cannot oxidize benzene, pyridine etc.
it is relatively a quick process
biodegradable matter cannot be distinguished from the rest
explain: The primary practical advantage of COD is the speed (3 hours vs 5 days), allowing for rapid monitoring and control of treatment plant processes.

q: 15. Presence of the following indicates recent pollution ...........
explain: Free ammonia or ammoniacal nitrogen is the first stage of nitrogen decomposition. Its presence indicates that the pollution occurred very recently and hasn't had time to oxidize into nitrites or nitrates.

q: 16. Presence of nitrogen in a waste water sample is due to the decomposition of ...........
explain: Proteins are complex organic compounds containing nitrogen. When proteins in sewage are decomposed by bacteria, they release nitrogen in various forms (ammonia, organic nitrogen).

q: 17. Combined system may be favoured where ............
options: rain fall is concentrated in a season of the year and D.W.F. is often fluctuating from day to day
rain fall is scattered throughout the year and D.W.F. is to small compared to storm water
rain fall is distributed throughout the year such that it is <= 10 * D.W.F.
city is on steep rocky slopes
explain: A combined sewer (carrying both sewage and storm water) works best when rainfall is frequent and predictable, keeping the sewers flushed.

q: 18. Separate system is adopted in ............
options: areas where rain fall is distributed throughout the year
explain: In areas with frequent rain, a separate system prevents the treatment plant from being overwhelmed by rainwater while still managing sewage.

q: 19. Partly separate system is ............
options: collecting D.W.F. and storm water in the same sewer
collecting D.W.F. and drainage of initial showers into the same sewer
collection of sewage and sullage into the same sewer
collection of storm water and a part of D.W.F. into the same sewer
explain: This system carries domestic sewage and the highly polluted 'first wash' of storm water in one pipe, while diverting clean excess rain to another.

q: 20. Leaping weir is provided only in ............
explain: A leaping weir is used in combined systems to allow dry weather flow to fall into an intercepting sewer while high-velocity storm water 'leaps' over it.

options: any waste water of domestic or industrial origin
explain: Sewage is the broad term for the liquid waste carried in sewers, originating from residential, commercial, and industrial activities.
Sullage refers specifically to domestic wastewater from kitchens and bathrooms that does not contain human excreta (night soil).

q: 23. Sewerage is ............
options: collection + conveyance + treatment + ultimate disposal of sewage
explain: Sewerage is the complete science and infrastructure covering the entire path of waste from the point of origin to final disposal.

q: 24. A sanitary sewer is expected to run ............
explain: Sanitary sewers are usually designed to run half-full at maximum discharge to provide space for ventilation and prevent overflows.

q: 25. Top space is left free in a sanitary sewer for ............
explain: Leaving space in the upper part of the pipe allows the system to accommodate sudden increases in flow volume without surging.

q: 26. Maximum flow in sewers may be taken as ............
explain: For design purposes, the peak or maximum flow is typically estimated as three times the average daily flow.

q: 27. In general 'Imperviousness' of any catchment shall be between ............
explain: The runoff coefficient varies based on surface type; a fully paved city might approach 95%, while a park might be as low as 1%.

q: 28. Time of concentration depends on ............
explain: Time of concentration (the time for water to travel from the farthest point to the outlet) is heavily influenced by the slope of the land.

q: 29. Velocity of flow in a sewer should be between ............
explain: Sewers need a 'self-cleansing' velocity of at least 0.6 m/s to prevent settling, but must stay below 3 m/s to prevent erosion of the pipe material.

q: 30. For a partly running circular sewer as the depth of flow increases ............
explain: As the depth of water in a pipe increases (up to a certain point), the cross-sectional area of flow increases, which increases the total discharge (Q).

q: 31. Ovoid sewers are best suited for ............
options: combined system with very wide fluctuations
explain: Ovoid (egg-shaped) sewers maintain a better velocity during low-flow periods (dry weather) compared to circular pipes, making them ideal for systems with high variation.

q: 32. Sewer that collects sewage from toilets is called ............
explain: A lateral sewer is the first stage of the network, collecting sewage directly from individual house connections (toilets/sinks) and carrying it to a branch sewer.

q: 33. The length of the main sewer leading to treatment of disposal units is called ............
explain: The outfall sewer is the final length of the sewerage system that conveys the entire accumulated volume of sewage to the treatment plant or the point of final disposal.

q: 34. A manhole is provided ............
explain: Manholes are essential points of access for inspection and cleaning; they must be placed wherever there is a change in the sewer's alignment, gradient, or pipe diameter.

q: 35. When fall in elevation is greater than 90 cm the manhole provided is called ............
explain: A drop manhole is used when a branch sewer enters a main sewer at a significantly higher elevation, preventing splashing and protecting the manhole structure from erosion.

q: 36. A fight sewer is provided when the gradient is ............
explain: In steep terrain, sewers must follow the slope while maintaining manageable velocities; specialized designs or 'flight' steps are used to manage the energy of the flow.

q: 37. When more than 2 sewers join in a manhole ............
options: their tops should be at the same level
their centres should be that the same level
their bottoms should be at the same level
explain: To maintain a smooth hydraulic profile and prevent backflow under pressure, the soffits (tops) of all incoming pipes should ideally be aligned with the soffit of the outgoing pipe.

q: 38. The working chamber of a manhole, along the direction of flow should have a minimum length of ............
explain: A minimum length of 1.2 m is required to provide enough space for a worker to enter, stand, and use tools comfortably for maintenance.

q: 39. 'Never discharge the contents of a bigger sewer into a smaller though the capacity of the later may be more due to steep slope' because ............
explain: Bigger sewers carry larger solids; if these enter a smaller pipe, they are much more likely to become lodged at the junction or in the pipe, causing a blockage.

q: 40. Before entering a manhole a candle is lowered into the manhole ............
options: to give a signal to the adjacent manhole
to find out presence of oxygen
explain: This is a traditional safety test; if the candle flame goes out, it indicates a lack of oxygen or a high concentration of non-combustible gases like CO2, making it unsafe to enter.

q: 41. A lamphole is helpful in ............
explain: A lamphole allows a light to be lowered into the sewer; by looking through the adjacent manhole, inspectors can check for obstructions or misalignments in the pipe.

q: 42. A syphon spillway is an arrangement to ............
options: divert excessive D.W.F. into open drain
divert excessive storm water into drain
divert excessive combine flow water into drain
explain: In combined systems, syphon spillways act as automatic relief valves to divert excess water (mixture of sewage and storm water) to a nearby watercourse during heavy rain.

q: 43. Colour of fresh sewage is ............
explain: Fresh sewage is typically a light grey or soapy color. As it becomes 'stale' or septic over time, it turns dark grey and eventually black.

q: 44. Sewage sickness is a sickness developed by ............
options: humans due to consumption of crops grown on sewage
plants because to harmful elements of sewage irrigation
land unable to accept any more loading of sewage
sewage itself due to pathogens within
explain: If too much sewage is applied to land without rest, the soil pores become clogged (anaerobic), preventing air from reaching roots and causing the land to become 'sick' and unproductive.

q: 45. An ideal crop of sewage irrigation is ............
explain: Crops like bananas are ideal because the edible part is high above the ground and protected by a skin, minimizing health risks compared to root vegetables or low-lying greens.

q: 46. When raw sewage is to be disposed off by dilution sewage should ............
options: be having a B.O.D. less than 150 mg/l
explain: Floating matter (grease, plastics, corks) creates an immediate aesthetic nuisance in rivers or lakes, so these must be removed via screening before dilution.

q: 47. Grit chamber had a detention period of ............
explain: Grit chambers are designed to remove heavy inorganic solids very quickly (usually in about 60 seconds) before they can reach and damage downstream pumps or treatment units.

q: 48. Velocity of flow through a grit chamber is ............
explain: The velocity is kept low enough (approx 0.3 m/s) to allow sand and grit to settle, but high enough to keep organic matter in suspension.

q: 49. Grit obtained in a grit chamber is used ............
explain: Because grit is largely composed of inorganic sand and gravel, it can be washed and reused in construction or as a fill material.

q: 50. The factor governing the detention period in a grit chamber is ............
explain: The detention time is calculated based on how long it takes for a particle to travel the length of the chamber at a specific horizontal flow velocity.
